issues.body:
In `trace_label` the new suffix is appended whenever `patterns.len() >= 3 && crate::dp::active().is_some()`, independent of the `plan` variable computed one line above from `bgp_uses_binary(&patterns)`.

The DP planner is only reachable from `eval_bgp_binary` (the `#[cfg(feature = "dp-planner")] if let Some(cfg) = crate::dp::active()` block at exec.rs:6952 sits inside that function). A BGP for which `bgp_uses_binary` is false is dispatched to the worst-case-optimal Leapfrog Triejoin path (exec.rs:3940, exec.rs:4858) and never reaches the DP at all. So for a cyclic 3+-pattern BGP the label becomes `BGP [worst-case-optimal (LFTJ)] (n patterns, m filters) [DPccp may execute; displayed tree is a greedy replay, not an execution record]` — a disclosure about a planner that cannot run on that plan, on a tree that is not a greedy replay either.

This label is not internal: it is the ANALYZE trace node label and, via `trace_label_pub` (exec.rs:4633), the `operator` string of the structured explain-json PlanNode (explain_json.rs:257,265) — both now exercised by default in the shipped server.

The companion change in explain.rs gets this right: `render_conjunctive` returns early on the `!exec::bgp_uses_binary(&patterns)` branch (explain.rs:289-312) before reaching the NOTE, so the text renderer never emits the disclosure for a cyclic BGP. The two renderers touched by this PR therefore disagree, and the inaccurate one is exactly the honesty surface the PR is meant to fix.
issues.fix_hint: Reuse the already-computed binary-plan decision instead of recomputing an unrelated condition, e.g. hoist `let uses_binary = bgp_uses_binary(&patterns);`, use it for `plan`, and gate the suffix on `uses_binary && patterns.len() >= 3 && crate::dp::active().is_some()`. Add a `#[cfg(feature = "dp-planner")]` engine test that EXPLAIN ANALYZE of a cyclic 3-pattern BGP (LFTJ) does NOT contain "DPccp may execute", alongside the existing positive case — a mutation flipping the gate back must turn that test red.
issues.title: DPccp disclosure is emitted for cyclic (LFTJ) BGPs where DPccp can never execute

issues.body:
The file is presented as a "compile-time tripwire for the server's `dp-planner` forwarding edge", but the file-level `#![cfg(feature = "dp-planner")]` means that removing `dp-planner` from sparq-server's `default` set compiles the whole file away and every lane stays green — the tripwire cannot trip on the regression it names. The doc comment is honest about this, but the test then provides no regression protection while reading as if it does.

The in-repo precedent works differently: `crates/sparq-cli/tests/cli_contract.rs::antijoin_static_decline_is_lit` and `algebra_rewrite_pass_is_lit_and_fires_on_iri_equality` are NOT cfg-gated, so dropping the feature from the CLI's `sparq-engine` dep line is a hard compile failure in `cargo test -p sparq-cli`.

Separately, the doc comment states "This file is gated on the server feature so deliberate lean builds remain valid" — the actual gate is `dp-planner`, not `server`, and the test never touches the server (it calls `sparq_engine::query` / `without_dp_planner` directly). The stated rationale does not match the code.

Also note the equivalence assertion is smoke-level: if DPccp silently declined this BGP, `planned` and `greedy` would be trivially equal and the test would still pass. The doc acknowledges this, but combined with the gate the file's net regression value is close to zero.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) fix the doc to say the gate is `dp-planner` and drop the "tripwire" framing, or (b) make it a real witness: keep an UNGATED test asserting `assert!(cfg!(feature = "dp-planner"))` in a module compiled only when the lean opt-out features are absent, or reference a `dp`-only symbol from an ungated test the way cli_contract.rs does. To de-smoke the equivalence check, assert DPccp actually accepted the BGP (e.g. expose a decline/accept counter under `dp-planner` the way `theta_antijoin_testing::early_declined` is exposed) so a silent decline fails the test.
issues.title: File-level `#![cfg(feature = "dp-planner")]` defeats the tripwire; doc comment misstates the gate

issues.body:
`antijoin-static-decline` is added to sparq-server's `default` set and forwarded to `sparq-engine/antijoin-static-decline`, and both crates/sparq-server/README.md and skills/http-server/SKILL.md now advertise it as default-on. Unlike `dp-planner` (which at least got `tests/dp_planner_default.rs`) and unlike the CLI (`cli_contract.rs::antijoin_static_decline_is_lit`, which references `sparq_engine::theta_antijoin_testing::early_declined` so the dep line cannot silently drop the feature), nothing in this PR pins the server's forwarding edge. A future edit to the `default` line silently un-does the documented behaviour while the docs continue to claim it.

The feature comment also says only "Match the CLI's static, result-equivalent early decline for anti-join shapes that cannot use the theta anti-join path" without pointing at where its equivalence witnesses live, whereas the adjacent `algebra-rewrite` comment names its feature-matrix leg and its CLI tripwire.
issues.fix_hint: Mirror `cli_contract.rs::antijoin_static_decline_is_lit` in sparq-server: an (ideally ungated) test that references `sparq_engine::theta_antijoin_testing::early_declined()` so dropping the feature from the `default` line breaks compilation in `cargo test -p sparq-server`. Extend the Cargo.toml comment to name the `sparq-engine (antijoin-static-decline)` feature-matrix leg that carries the equivalence witnesses, as the `algebra-rewrite` comment does.
issues.title: `antijoin-static-decline` joins the binary default with no forwarding tripwire or test

issues.body:
This PR turns on, by default, a planner whose enumeration is explicitly documented as not polling the QueryBudget cancellation/deadline. The work is bounded — `plan()` bails when `count_csg` exceeds `max_subgraphs` (4096) and `enumerate_csg_cmp_pairs` aborts past `max_subgraphs * PAIR_BUDGET_FACTOR` (524 288 emitted pairs) — but within that bound it is a fixed, uninterruptible chunk of CPU plus a multi-MB `pairs` allocation, a sort, and up to that many `JoinTree` clones, all before the cooperative deadline can take effect. On the network-facing binary a short adversarial BGP therefore buys a guaranteed, non-cancellable planning cost per request that `query_timeout` cannot cut short (it can only guarantee the 503, per the doc on `Config::query_timeout` in http.rs).

The trade-off IS disclosed — in the Cargo.toml feature comment, in this README bullet, and in the SKILL blockquote — but only inside a bullet framed as "measured-plan parity", with the hardening note appended as a trailing clause. The README has a dedicated "Security posture (essentials)" section directly below, which is where an operator evaluating a public deployment will actually look, and it says nothing about this.
issues.fix_hint: Add one line to the "Security posture (essentials)" section (and the corresponding SKILL section) stating that default-on `dp-planner` performs bounded but non-cancellable join-order planning before the query deadline applies, and naming `--no-default-features --features server,jsonld` as the hardening opt-out. Alternatively, consider polling the budget between csg/cmp emission batches so planning honours the deadline, which would remove the caveat rather than document it.
issues.title: Non-cancellable planning cost is a default-on availability trade-off but is absent from the Security posture section

issues.body: `patterns.len() >= 3` mirrors the lower bound of `dp::plan`'s `if !(3..=MAX_PATTERNS).contains(&n)` guard but not the upper bound (`MAX_PATTERNS = 63`). A BGP with more than 63 patterns is always planned greedily, yet still gets the "DPccp may execute" suffix. The hedged "may" wording makes this not a false statement, and 63+ pattern BGPs are rare, but the predicate is now a partial duplicate of the planner's own admission rule and will drift if `MAX_PATTERNS` or the lower bound changes.
issues.fix_hint: Express the condition once — e.g. a `pub(crate) fn dp_may_plan(n: usize) -> bool` in dp.rs used by `plan()`, by `trace_label`, and by `render_conjunctive` — so the disclosure and the admission rule cannot diverge.
issues.title: Disclosure predicate mirrors only the lower half of `dp::plan`'s pattern-count guard

verdict.summary:
The core of the change is sound: `dp-planner`/`antijoin-static-decline` exist as real sparq-engine features (Cargo.toml:172,208), the parity claim checks out (sparq-cli/Cargo.toml:146 already enables all three on its sparq-engine dep), the engine library default stays OFF, no dependency is added, and the feature-off declaration file matches the mechanism scripts/check-vectorized-feature-off.py expects. DPccp result-equivalence is pre-existing and covered by crates/sparq-engine/tests/dp_default.rs, and planning is bounded (count_csg cap + PAIR_BUDGET_FACTOR pair cap), so enabling it server-side does not change answers. The new explain disclosure in explain.rs is correctly placed after the LFTJ early-return, i.e. only on the binary path where DPccp can actually run.

One blocking defect: the sibling disclosure in exec.rs `trace_label` is NOT gated on `bgp_uses_binary`, so a cyclic BGP routed to Leapfrog Triejoin — a path where DPccp provably never executes (the DP block lives inside `eval_bgp_binary`, exec.rs:6952) — is still labelled "DPccp may execute" in the ANALYZE trace and in the structured explain-json `operator` field. The two renderers this PR touches therefore disagree with each other, and the inaccurate one is the user-facing honesty surface the PR exists to fix.

Secondary: the new `dp_planner_default.rs` carries a file-level `#![cfg(feature = "dp-planner")]` that defeats its own compile-time tripwire (its doc also misdescribes the gate as the `server` feature), and `antijoin-static-decline` joins the server default with no tripwire at all, unlike the in-repo precedent in sparq-cli/tests/cli_contract.rs. The non-cancellable planning cost is documented with an opt-out but is absent from the server README's Security posture section.
